- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 3x recent high or 2x prior peak for 30d.
- If sentiment is positive and price history shows mean reversion (e.g., recent 5-day decline), model overreacts; apply 10–20% downward adjustment.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is below 0.5 and sentiment is neutral or positive, model is too optimistic; apply 20–40% downward bias.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.33–1.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., > 2x difference), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, model may be overfitting to sentiment; reduce forecast by 30–50% if sentiment > 0.7.
- For 30d forecasts, if model shows high volatility (e.g., > 3 standard deviations from mean), reduce forecast magnitude by 20–30% to align with sentiment stability.
